title: FSD S3 reads the ACE views directly, while Architecture v5 allows only rwb-source-data to read them
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13, 37 and 45; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 DP-05
section: A1.1 constraints; A2.1 to A2.8 validation rules VR-S3-001-1 to VR-S3-008-1
description: The FSD states that source data is read only from the SELECT-only recovery.v_ace_* views, landed by ACE's own ingestion, with no inbound load in the Workbench, and every one of the eight features carries a validation rule that reads freshness from v_ace_batch_status. Arch v5 slide 37 changes '30 views read by any module (ADR-010)' to views read only by rwb-source-data, slide 45 answers 'who reads ACE data' with rwb-source-data alone and adds that everyone else asks it through REST or a Temporal activity, and slide 13 gives the S3 row no cell to P1. The Ownership Map records no view and no data product for S3. The read path of this service is therefore undefined in the FSD, and so is the freshness response behind MSG-P1-001.
evidence: FSD S3 A1.1 constraints (SELECT-only views, no inbound load, D-RCV-35) and A2.1.3.1, A2.2.3.1, A2.3.3.1, A2.4.3.1, A2.5.3.1, A2.7.3.1 VR-S3-00x-1 (v_ace_batch_status, MSG-P1-001). Arch v5 slide 13 (S3 row: T to P7, T E to P6, E from P8; no P1, P2 or P10 cell), slide 37, slide 45. Rules DP-05. Ownership Map: Services row S3; Tables sheet has no S3 view or data product.
proposed: Carry the FSD field names as the source field names that the rwb-source-data contract returns and build every claim read on that contract; this service reads no view and no ACE table. Confirm the contract fields and the freshness response with P1 before wave 3 system test.

title: The claim submission has no interface: INT-29 is not available today and the S3 row has no call to an outside system
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6); Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5, TSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v2 T5.1 (INT-29); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3.md integrations sheet; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 13; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1
section: A2.2 Submit the claim to the TCG portal; A1.2 FEAT-GUA-02
description: FSD A2.2 gives the feature the actor 'System', rule R-GUA-12 submits the claim through the TCG claim channel and A2.2.2 names the TCG portal as the integration point. TSD S3 T5.1 makes INT-29 'Both, not available today; entered and filed by the guarantee officer, as needed' and the Epics 3 to 8 integration sheet repeats that wording. Arch v5 slide 13 gives the S3 row no cell to P2 and no cell to Outside, and the Ownership Map has no interface row for S3. The product behaviour 'the system files the claim' therefore has no confirmed channel, and whether the officer files outside the Workbench and the reference is recorded is not stated either.
evidence: FSD S3 A1.2 FEAT-GUA-02, A2.2.2 integration points (TCG portal), A2.2.3.1 R-GUA-12. TSD S3 v2 T5.1 INT-29 ('Not available today; entered and filed by the guarantee officer'). Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 integrations sheet INT-29 (Thai Credit Guarantee Corporation, quota and claim submission, Both). Arch v5 slide 13 S3 row. Ownership Map Endpoints sheet: S3 has POST and PATCH only.
owner_role: Solution architect with the integration lead
proposed: Record the submission reference, the submission date and the channel used on the claim, and let that record move the claim to CLAIM_SUBMITTED; an interface through rwb-integration is added when INT-29 becomes available, and until then the officer's entry is the submission event. Confirm with the integration lead before wave 3 system test.

title: The claim is assembled by an agent that has no call path from this service
source: Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 19 and its open decisions list; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 13; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 DP-20; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1
section: A2.1 Prepare a TCG guarantee claim; R-GUA-04
description: R-GUA-04 states 'The claim preparation agent assembles the claim against the scheme checklist' and step 2 of the Temporal and Drools design slide 19 carries the AI agent symbol, with the rule package at Phase 2. Arch v5 slide 13 gives the S3 row no cell to P10 and the Ownership Map names no S3 workflow activity on rwb-agent, while DP-20 gives every service the agent contract as a C dependency. The agent's role in this service is therefore stated in the rules and unconfirmed in the call graph, and the fallback when the agent is slow or its output fails the schema check (NFR-024, NFR-055) is not stated for the claim.
evidence: Routing Logic v4 R-GUA-04. Temporal and Drools Design v1 slide 19 (step 2 'Agent assembles claim' R-GUA-04, AI agent legend) and its open decisions list item 3 (Drools packages for S1 and S3 to S9 are Phase 2). Arch v5 slide 13 S3 row (no P10 cell). Rules DP-20. Ownership Map Workflows sheet: GuaranteeClaimWorkflow, S3; no agent activity row.
owner_role: Solution architect with the P10 owner
proposed: Call the agent through the rwb-agent contract as a Temporal activity on rwb-guarantee, take the checklist result when the agent does not answer inside 60 seconds or fails the schema check, and record which of the two assembled the claim.

title: The claim status list has five values while the claim workflow has seventeen states, and no mapping is given
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6); Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5, TSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v2 T3.2 and T4; Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4
section: A2.6.3.2 and A2.8.3.2 field catalog (status); TSD T3.2 LOV-CLAIM-STATUS and T4 GUARANTEE state machine
description: The FSD and the TSD give guarantee_claim.status as varchar(12) on LOV-CLAIM-STATUS with five values (PREPARING, FILED, DEFECT, PAID, REJECTED), and the TSD T4 and the Routing Logic v4 give the claim 32 rules over 17 states (GUARANTEE_DETECTED, NOT_ELIGIBLE, DEADLINE_TIMER_RUNNING, CLAIM_PREPARATION, CLAIM_DEFECT_HOLD, CLAIM_APPROVAL, CLAIM_SUBMITTED, TCG_QUERY, CLAIM_REJECTED, CLAIM_PART_PAID, CLAIM_PAID, SUBROGATION_POSITION, GUARANTOR_NOTICE, GUARANTOR_DISPUTE_HOLD, DEADLINE_MISSED, GUARANTEE_CLOSED, RESIDUAL_TO_ROUTE). No source states how one maps to the other, which one the case and the screen show, or which one a report counts.
evidence: FSD S3 A2.6.3.2 and A2.8.3.2 field catalog row guarantee_claim.status (varchar(12), LOV-CLAIM-STATUS). TSD S3 v2 T3.2 (LOV-CLAIM-STATUS, five values) and T4 (32 rules over 17 states). Routing Logic v4 R-GUA-01 to R-GUA-32 with their from-states and to-states.
owner_role: Business analyst, S3 with the P7 owner
proposed: Make the workflow state the state of record and derive the published claim status from it at each transition, with the mapping held as versioned reference data; publish both on the claim so a report and the case agree.

title: The guarantee, the guarantor pursuit and the subrogation position have no owned record
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 18 and 41; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 Tables; Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5, TSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v2 T3.1 and T3.3; Recovery Workbench FSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-GUA-23, R-GUA-24, R-GUA-28, R-GUA-29
section: Service contract (S3 OUT); A2.6 Negotiate with a guarantor; A2.4 Record the subrogation position
description: Arch v5 slides 18 and 41 state that schema rwb_guarantee holds 'TCG and insurance claims, guarantor notices and pursuit'. The Ownership Map Tables sheet has one S3 row, guarantee_claim, and the TSD S3 T3.1 defines that one object with eight fields (DF-TRT-015 to DF-TRT-022) whose only cross-reference is case_id. R-GUA-23 and R-GUA-24 record the TCG share 'against the case for all future recoveries', R-GUA-28 books a treatment and reduces the balance, R-GUA-29 records the refusal 'against the party', and FSD A2.6 asks for the outcome to be recorded against the party. No field and no object holds the guarantee itself, the guarantor party, the guaranteed amount, the TCG share or the pursuit outcome, although three of the eight features and two of the four BRD requirements need one.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 18 ('DB writes schema rwb_guarantee: TCG and insurance claims, guarantor notices and pursuit') and slide 41 (S3 row). Ownership Map Tables: guarantee_claim, owner S3; no other S3 row. TSD S3 v2 T3.1 guarantee_claim (eight fields) and T3.3 (one relationship, case_id). FSD S3 A2.6.3.2 and A2.8.3.2 field catalog. Routing Logic v4 R-GUA-23, R-GUA-24, R-GUA-28, R-GUA-29.
proposed: State the guarantee, the guarantor pursuit and the subrogation share as entity groups named after Arch v5 slide 18, give the claim record only the fields the sources confirm, and fix the physical table set with the S3 DB story; add the missing rows to the Ownership Map in the same change.

title: The guarantor notice feature names no notice rule and no field set
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4; Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5, TSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v2 T4; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 19; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 18 and 41
section: A2.5 Notify guarantors and co-borrowers (FEAT-GUA-05, REQ-S3-004)
description: FSD A2.5 lists only VR-S3-005-1 (stale product) and BR-S3-005 (no value in code) and has no field catalog, so it states no template, no recipient set, no notice period and no rule that selects any of them. The rules that govern the notice sit elsewhere: R-GUA-06 (GUARANTOR_NOTICE_DUE, guarantee_type in personal guarantor, co-borrower or corporate) and R-GUA-28 to R-GUA-32 in the Routing Logic v4 and the TSD T4, and the Temporal and Drools design slide 19 says the guarantor notice runs in parallel with proof of delivery. Arch v5 gives the notice itself to rwb-comms, which leaves the trigger, the recipient set and the period as this service's behaviour with no requirement text.
evidence: FSD S3 A2.5.3.1 (VR-S3-005-1, BR-S3-005 only) and the absence of an A2.5.3.2 field catalog. Routing Logic v4 R-GUA-06, R-GUA-28, R-GUA-29, R-GUA-30, R-GUA-31, R-GUA-32. TSD S3 v2 T4 (GUARANTOR_NOTICE and GUARANTOR_DISPUTE_HOLD states). Temporal and Drools Design v1 slide 19 notes ('Guarantor notice runs in parallel (R-GUA-06)'; 'D6.6 guarantor notice in parallel (R-GUA-06, EV-13/14/15)'). Arch v5 slide 41 (P6 owns notices, templates, merge fields, proof of delivery).
owner_role: Business analyst, S3 with the P6 owner
proposed: Write the notice behaviour from R-GUA-06 and R-GUA-28 to R-GUA-32: the recipient set from the parties on the case, the template from the approved set in rwb-comms, the period from proof of delivery, and the answer that returns to the route decision.

title: Two rule pairs repeat and one submission rule appears under claim tracking
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.3 and A2.4; Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4; Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5, TSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v2 T4
description: R-GUA-23 and R-GUA-24 carry identical text ('Record the TCG share against the case for all future recoveries') with different from-states (CLAIM_PAID and CLAIM_PART_PAID). R-GUA-05 and R-GUA-09 both move to DEADLINE_MISSED with near-identical text from different states. FSD A2.3 (Track the claim to payment) lists R-GUA-12, which is the submission rule of A2.2, as one of its own. The sources do not say whether each pair is one rule with two from-states or two independent rules, which matters for the rule count (32) and for the package that is versioned in P7.
evidence: FSD S3 A2.3.3.1 (R-GUA-05, R-GUA-09, R-GUA-12) and A2.4.3.1 (R-GUA-22, R-GUA-23, R-GUA-24). Routing Logic v4 and TSD S3 v2 T4 rows for the same rule IDs; Temporal and Drools Design v1 slide 19 ('Guarantee route set, 32 rules').
proposed: Keep both from-states of each pair in the guarantee rule package and count the package as 32 rules until the authoring owner confirms the split.

title: The insurance claim is Must in the epic BRD but has no program requirement
source: 03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1.md section 8.2 (BR-025); 03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5.md section 5.10; Recovery Workbench FSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) Requirements served; Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5, TSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v2 T8
section: BR-025; REQ-S3-001 to REQ-S3-007; FSD A2.8
description: BR-025 (Must; FEAT-GUA-08, RWB-E4-020) requires that a collateral event files an insurance claim and triggers a re-appraisal before the next decision. The Program BRD section 5.10 holds seven requirements and none of them names the insurance claim, the FSD 'Requirements served' table repeats the same seven, and the TSD T8 maps all seven to FEAT-GUA-01. The feature exists in the FSD with a field catalog and an acceptance criterion placeholder, so a Must behaviour has no program requirement to trace to.
evidence: Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 section 8.2 BR-025 (source column: FEAT-GUA-08; RWB-E4-020) and section 14 traceability. Business Requirements Program v5 section 5.10 (REQ-S3-001 to REQ-S3-007). FSD S3 A1.2 FEAT-GUA-08, A2.8, Requirements served (seven rows). TSD S3 v2 T8 (all seven rows mapped to FEAT-GUA-01).
proposed: Trace the insurance claim through BR-025 and REQ-S3-002 (claim status on the case) and raise a program requirement for the collateral event when the program requirement set is next versioned.

title: The release of a guarantor and of a TCG guarantee have approval authorities but no requirement
source: Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 19 and DoA rows; 03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1.md Q-001; 03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5.md DL18; Recovery Workbench FSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6)
section: Temporal and Drools design slide 19 ('Who approves', 'Release guarantor', 'Release TCG guarantee')
description: The Temporal and Drools design slide 19 states 'Release guarantor: L4 ≤ THB 30m, L3 ≤ THB 200m' and 'Release TCG guarantee: PARC', and its notes cite the existing capabilities 2.1.5 (release a guarantor) and 2.4 (release a TCG guarantee). No FSD feature, no acceptance criterion and no BR names a release, and the limits it quotes are the policy values that DL18 and BRD Q-001 leave open. A behaviour that releases a guarantor from a debt therefore has an approval authority in a design document and no product requirement, and the authority it names cannot be tested against a value.
evidence: Temporal and Drools Design v1 slide 19 ('Release guarantor: L4 ≤ THB 30m, L3 ≤ THB 200m'; 'Release TCG guarantee: PARC'; notes citing 2.1.5 and 2.4). Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 Q-001 and ASM-B-REQ-BRD-E38-1. Program BRD v5 DL18. FSD S3: no release feature and no release acceptance criterion.
legacy_ref: None; the release has no legacy story
proposed: Deliver the release through the approval path in rwb-decision with the level read from the delegation table, state the behaviour as a capability of this product, and keep the limits out of this document until DL18 answers them.

title: The claim read has no operation, although the architecture gives the service a GET
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 18; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench API Specification v4.yaml; Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5, TSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v2 T-A.1; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 Endpoints
section: Service contract (S3 IN); API-S3-001 and API-S3-002; SCR-17
description: Arch v5 slide 18 gives rwb-guarantee the inbound contract 'REST GET/POST /guarantee-claims'. The API Specification v4 defines POST /cases/{caseId}/guarantee-claims (operationId postCasesCaseidGuaranteeClaims) and PATCH /guarantee-claims/{claimId} (operationId patchGuaranteeClaimsClaimid) and no GET, the TSD T-A.1 mirrors those two operations, and the Ownership Map Endpoints sheet has the same two rows. Screen SCR-17 shows the guarantee, the claim deadline, the checklist and the claim result, which is a read of the claim that no published operation serves.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 18 (S3 IN: REST GET/POST /guarantee-claims). API Specification v4 paths /cases/{caseId}/guarantee-claims (post) and /guarantee-claims/{claimId} (patch); no get operation on either path. TSD S3 v2 T-A.1 API-S3-001, API-S3-002 and T-A.2. Ownership Map Endpoints: two S3 rows. FSD S3 Screens: SCR-17 Guarantee claim.
proposed: Add the claim read to the service contract before the contract story closes, on the path the gateway will call, and cite the operation in the screen and the case tab stories; no path is asserted in this document.

title: TSD S3 publishes no event, while Architecture v5 gives two claim events and the catalogue numbers neither
source: Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5, TSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v2 T5.3; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 18, 42 and 43; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Event and Messaging Design v4.md; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 Events
description: TSD S3 T5.3 states 'Events: None'. Arch v5 slide 18 gives topic rwb.guarantee.events.v1 with GuaranteeClaimFiled and GuaranteeClaimSettled, slide 43 lists 'TreatmentClosed, GuaranteeClaim*' as published by rwb-treatment and rwb-guarantee to rwb-case and rwb-reporting, and slide 41 names the topic in the service row. Neither event carries an EV number in the event catalogue, the Event and Messaging Design v4 stops at EV-19 and names no claim event, and the Ownership Map Events sheet has no S3 row, so the producer, the payload and the consumers of the two events are given in the architecture alone.
evidence: TSD S3 v2 T5.3 ('None'). Arch v5 slide 18 (OUT: topic rwb.guarantee.events.v1: GuaranteeClaimFiled, GuaranteeClaimSettled), slide 41 (S3 row: topic rwb.guarantee.events.v1), slide 42 (EV-01 to EV-19, no claim event), slide 43 ('+ TreatmentClosed, GuaranteeClaim* | rwb-treatment / guarantee | — | rwb-case, rwb-reporting'). Event and Messaging Design v4 event table (EV-10 to EV-19). Ownership Map Events: no S3 row.
legacy_ref: None; no legacy story names either event
proposed: Publish GuaranteeClaimFiled at submission and GuaranteeClaimSettled at payment or release, keyed by case, with identifiers and facts only, and add the two rows to the event catalogue and the Ownership Map when the numbers are allocated.

title: The TCG quota and the claim deadline for each scheme are not set
source: 03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1.md BR-022, Q-013 and ASM-020; 03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5.md section 5.10; Recovery Workbench FSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.1.3.1 (R-GUA-01); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4
description: BR-022 requires a claim filed inside the scheme deadline, R-GUA-01 starts the deadline timer from the date the default conditions are met when the guarantee type is the TCG scheme and a scheme code is present, R-GUA-04 compares the days remaining to the preparation window and R-GUA-11 compares them to the warning window. BRD Q-013 asks for the TCG quota and the claim deadline per scheme and ASM-020 records them as reference data per scheme with Low confidence; the FSD's field catalog holds claim_deadline as a date with no source, and no source holds a scheme table. Every deadline-driven behaviour of this service therefore rests on a value no source states.
evidence: Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 BR-022, Q-013 (owner role: Guarantee officer; blocks BR-022 and RULE-001), ASM-020 (Low confidence). Routing Logic v4 R-GUA-01, R-GUA-04, R-GUA-11. FSD S3 A2.1.3.1 and A2.6.3.2 (claim_deadline, date, required).
proposed: Load the deadline, the preparation window and the warning window as versioned reference data per scheme, read at run time, and hold this document to the rule that no value is restated.

title: The retention class and the masking rules of the claim record are not set
source: 03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5.md NFR-028, NFR-031, NFR-047, DL26; 03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1.md Q-012 and ASM-019; Recovery Workbench FSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) field catalog
section: A2.6.3.2 and A2.8.3.2 field catalog (claimed_amount, paid_amount); NFR-028, NFR-031, NFR-047
description: The claim holds the amount claimed and the amount paid, and the guarantor is a party to the debt with a name and a contact point reached through the notice. NFR-028 leaves the retention class periods unset, NFR-031 leaves the case-record retention and archive rule unset, NFR-047 leaves the classification scheme open and BRD Q-012 asks for the retention periods and the masking rules by record class and role (DL26). The claim record therefore has a classification of record in this document but no period and no masking row.
evidence: Program BRD v5 NFR-028, NFR-031, NFR-047 (Open, DL26) and DL26. Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 Q-012, ASM-019. FSD S3 A2.6.3.2 and A2.8.3.2 (claimed_amount, paid_amount in baht).
proposed: Apply a record class to the claim and to the guarantor record, hold the period as reference data, and mask the party fields by role once DL26 answers; no period is stated in this document.

title: No source fixes the screen ownership or the gateway route of SCR-17
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) Screens; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13, 18 and 41; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 DP-19
description: The FSD gives SCR-17 Guarantee claim as first in E4 and states what it shows, with no owning service and no route. Arch v5 slides 41 and 13 name services and call types and no screen, and DP-19 sends a screen through a gateway-bff composite route. The service that assembles the screen and the path the gateway calls are therefore open, as they are for SCR-13 in S1.
evidence: FSD S3 Screens (SCR-17 Guarantee claim, first in E4). Arch v5 slides 13, 18, 41 (no screen named). Rules DP-19 (gateway-bff composite route), RWB-PLT-N001-CON.
proposed: Serve SCR-17 as a gateway-bff composite route over this service's contract and the case contract, and record the owner and the route in the edge catalogue.

title: Four messages are shown without an owner for their wording
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) VR-S3-001-1 to VR-S3-008-1, AC-EXC-S3-001-01 to AC-EXC-S3-008-02; 03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5.md NFR-059
section: A2.1 to A2.8 validation tables and exception flows
description: MSG-P1-001 ({product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived.), MSG-P4-002 (role without the right), MSG-P7-003 (decision cannot be recorded) and MSG-GEN-001 (Enter {field}.) are shown by this service, and NFR-059 requires every label and message in Thai and in English. No source names the service that owns the wording of a shared message or the role that approves the two language versions.
evidence: FSD S3 VR-S3-001-1 to VR-S3-008-1 (MSG-P1-001, MSG-GEN-001) and AC-EXC-S3-001-01 to AC-EXC-S3-008-02 (MSG-P4-002, MSG-P7-003). Program BRD v5 NFR-059 (Thai and English, DL10).

title: The guarantee claim route has two numbers in the sources
source: Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-01; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 17 open point and open decisions list; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 3
section: Arch v5 slide 3 (eight routes); Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-01
description: R-LIT-01 starts litigation on route R4, while the case journeys call R4 the guarantee claim and R5 litigation; the Temporal and Drools design records the conflict as an open point on the S1 slide and again in its open decisions list. Arch v5 slide 3 names the route 'Guarantee claim' with no number. This service is the guarantee route, so the number it carries and the number a report counts are both unsettled.
evidence: Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-01 (route R4). Temporal and Drools Design v1 slide 17 open point ('route numbering conflicts between documents') and open decisions list item 4. Arch v5 slide 3 (eight routes, named, unnumbered).
owner_role: Business analyst, S3 with the P7 owner
proposed: Name the route 'guarantee claim' with no number in this document, and hold the number as reference data once the route numbering is agreed.

title: Every acceptance criterion of the FSD is a placeholder
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.1.4 to A2.8.4
section: A2.1.4.1 to A2.8.4.1 main success flows
description: AC-S3-001-01 to AC-S3-008-01 read 'The data and rules it needs are in place / The trigger arrives (or: The user acts) / The result is recorded with its rule version', and the story column reads 'Written one epic ahead' in every row. The exception rows AC-EXC-S3-00x-01 and AC-EXC-S3-00x-02 are identical across the eight features. No criterion therefore states a scenario, a value or an outcome that a test can assert, and the FSD states no alternate flow and no system background event for any feature.
evidence: FSD S3 A2.1.4.1 to A2.8.4.1 (eight main success rows), A2.1.4.2 to A2.8.4.2 ('None'), A2.1.4.3 to A2.8.4.3 (two generic exception rows each), A2.1.4.4 to A2.8.4.4 ('None').
proposed: Write each acceptance criterion in this document from the named rule and its message, keep the FSD criterion ID as its evidence, and return the written criteria to the FSD when it is next versioned.

title: The number of claims a month and the number of guarantors a case are not stated
source: 03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5.md NFR-001 and section 6.1; Recovery Workbench FSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6); 03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1.md
description: NFR-001 gives the case volume (about 23,600 open cases at go-live, 26,500 at the end of 2027, from 3,110 new accounts a month) and the guarantee claim is one of eight routes. No source gives the share of cases that carry a guarantee, the number of claims a month, the number of guarantors on a case, or the number of notices a demand produces, so the volume target of this service cannot be copied from a source and no count is recomputed here.
evidence: Program BRD v5 NFR-001 and section 6.1 (volume and capacity). FSD S3: no volume statement. Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1: no guarantee volume in section 10 (success measures).
proposed: State the volume target as the program case volume that this service inherits and carry the claim share as an open question until the business lead sets it.

title: The dates and change notes of FSD S3 v1 and v2 are not in the sources read
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) document control
description: The FSD v3 change note states that v3 is re-based on the ACE database and that 'everything else is unchanged from v2', and the copy read holds no v1 or v2 text, no date for either and no change note of its own. The earlier history of this module therefore cannot be carried into the product baseline beyond the v3 note, and the two versions are recorded as an open item rather than reconstructed from the v3 wording.
evidence: FSD S3 document control: Document ID S3-RWB-FSD-v3, Version 3, Date 15 November 2026, change note 'v3, 15 November 2026: re-based on the ACE database under D-RCV-35 (ADR-010) ... Everything else unchanged from v2'.
proposed: Carry the v3 note as the inherited change history of this module and record the two earlier versions as an open item until the FSD owner supplies them.
